core.title: Keep user/system flow and product capability references bidirectional (user/system flow - product capability Coverage)
core.given: A plan containing user/system flows and/or product capability manifests (either side may be empty), plus the plan's allow-list of product capabilities exempt from user/system flow membership
core.when: the planner adds, removes, renames, or changes the status of a product capability manifest; adds, removes, or edits a user/system flow's participants; or changes the exemption allow-list
core.then: Keep user/system-flow-capability coverage bidirectional with no orphan: every product capability appears in at least one user/system flow's participants (product capability -> user/system flow), and every product capability reference in a user/system flow's participants resolves to a product capability manifest (user/system flow -> product capability).
prefer: When creating a product capability manifest, add it as a participant of at least one user/system flow in the same change.
When adding a product capability reference to a user/system flow's participants, create or point to an existing product capability manifest in the same change.
When renaming or removing a product capability, update every user/system flow participant that references it.
When removing a product capability from the exemption allow-list or promoting it out of draft status, add it to a user/system flow in the same change.
avoid: Leaving an orphan on either side: a product capability in no user/system flow, or a user/system flow participant with no product capability manifest.
Adding a product capability to the exemption allow-list or marking it draft just to silence the coverage check.
unless: product capability -> user/system flow direction only: the product capability is listed in the exemption allow-list or has draft status.
core.why: Bidirectional coverage means each side references the other with no orphan: every non-exempt product capability is reachable from a user/system flow, and every product capability reference in a user/system flow resolves to a product capability manifest.
evidence: The product capability -> user/system flow coverage check passes: every product capability appears in at least one user/system flow's participants, excepting allow-listed or draft product capabilities.
The user/system flow -> product capability coverage check passes: every product capability reference in a user/system flow's participants has a product capability manifest.
verification: Two independent direction checks: product capability -> user/system flow requires every product capability manifest to appear in at least one user/system flow's participants; user/system flow -> product capability requires every product capability participant reference to resolve to a product capability manifest. Each check fires even when the other side (user/system flows or product capabilities) is empty.
Exceptions apply to the product capability -> user/system flow direction only (the exemption allow-list and draft status); the user/system flow -> product capability direction has no exceptions.

Scope: the checks cover capability/user-system-flow reference structure only; edits to product capability content that do not change product capability identity, status, allow-list membership, or user/system flow participants are not covered.

values: product capability status changed from draft
product capability removed from the exemption allow-list
product capability -> user/system flow coverage check failure
user/system flow -> product capability coverage check failure

fires: Planner adds a new non-draft product capability manifest, not listed in the exemption allow-list, that no user/system flow lists in its participants.
Planner adds a product capability manifest while the plan has no user/system flows at all, and the product capability is neither draft nor in the exemption allow-list.
Planner adds a product capability reference to a user/system flow for which no product capability manifest exists (including when the plan has no product capability manifests).
Planner renames or deletes a product capability manifest still referenced by a user/system flow participant.
Planner removes or edits a user/system flow so that a non-draft, non-allow-listed product capability is no longer in any user/system flow.
Planner promotes a product capability out of draft status without adding it to any user/system flow, and it is not in the exemption allow-list.
Planner removes from the exemption allow-list a non-draft product capability that is not in any user/system flow.
doesNotFire: A product capability with draft status is not yet in any user/system flow.
A product capability listed in the exemption allow-list is not in any user/system flow.
Edits to product capability content (features, DESIRED OUTCOMES, acceptances) that do not change product capability identity, status, allow-list membership, or user/system flow participants.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds this rule reads: the user/system flow artifacts, the product capability manifests, and the product capability exemption allow-list (the artifact whose entries exempt a product capability from user/system flow membership).
How a user/system flow's participant entry refers to a product capability — the reference whose resolution the user/system flow -> product capability direction checks.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a user/system flow participant entry beginning with `capability:` (the `capability:` participant)

profileRequirements.meaning: How the plan marks a product capability manifest as draft, i.e. not yet required to be in a user/system flow.
profileRequirements.bunValue: status:draft on the product capability manifest

neutralityNotes: The convention is a plan-model rule, so it is almost fully neutral already. 'user/system flow', 'product capability', 'DESIRED OUTCOME', 'feature' and 'acceptance' are plan-artifact concepts present in the closed vocabulary (urn artifacts), not stack terms, and are kept. Three concrete bindings come from the profile: the plan-artifact kind names incl. the exemption allow-list (roles.plan_artifact.kinds: capabilities_not_in_user_system_flow_allow_list), the product capability reference syntax in a user/system flow's participants (urn.capability: the `capability:` prefix), and the draft status spelling (proposed idiom.plan_syntax#capability_draft_status: status:draft). The two validator ids (test_all_capabilities_in_at_least_one_user_system_flow, test_all_user_system_flow_capability_refs_exist) and the finding ids are Bun realization details kept in bunOnly; core.verification describes the two direction checks generically, including that each fires even when the opposite side is empty, that exceptions apply only to the product capability -> user/system flow direction, and the documentation-only disposition.
